---
title: "The cost of LLMs vs humans"
claim: "LLMs are almost always cheaper than humans"
---

**LLMs are almost always cheaper than humans.**

@metr2024capability compare the cost of humans and LLMs to do a variety of tasks, they say “when agents *can* do a task, they can often do so at a fraction of the cost of humans.”

![From @metr2024capability](images/image16.png){.column-margin}

Similarly @metr2025gpt5evaluation finds:

![Agent Performance on HCAST & RE-Bench by Cost](images/2025-09-19-16-04-34.png){.column-margin}

Exceptions:

- Computer transcription was for a period more accurate but less cost-effective than humans.
- Reasoning tasks with high test-time expenditure ([ARC-AGI](https://arcprize.org/arc-agi)))
- [Svanberg et al. (2024)](https://futuretech-site.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/2024-01-18+Beyond_AI_Exposure.pdf) argue that "only 23% of worker compensation “exposed” to AI computer vision would be cost-effective for firms to automate because of the large upfront costs of AI systems." However this is almost entirely fixed costs (data collection, fine tuning, scaffolding), not marginal costs.
